phrase.text: PseudoLearn deliberately leaves out some pieces of other object languages, and when it recognises them it explains so with a message of its own.

runs.text: PseudoLearn deliberately leaves out some pieces of other object languages, and when it recognises them it explains so with a message of its own.

blocks.description: Four constructs that do not exist, each with its alternative: abstract classes versus interfaces, static members versus parameters, protected versus Public and Private, and exceptions versus Result.

caption.text: The four constructs that are recognised to explain that they do not exist, and what PseudoLearn offers instead.

runs.text: The engine recognises their typical forms
—for example, one more word in a class header— and gives a teaching message instead of a generic error. Those words
: they can be used as names anywhere else.

blocks.title: A static member
blocks.source:
Class Contador
  Estatico Define total As Integer;
EndClass

Algorithm Mal
EndAlgorithm

diagnostics.message: Static members are not supported in PseudoLearn

runs.text: For expected errors, the language uses values:
. To share data between objects, it is passed as parameters.

points.text: There are no abstract classes, static members, protected or exceptions.
Their typical forms produce a message of their own.
